justification: The scan confirms a superfluous s, and the same index prints Digressione on p. XIII, so the intended word is certain and deleting one letter corrects it.
Since F is itself the transform of f, the context makes trasformata di f certain, and changing one letter corrects it.
The scan confirms a spurious line-end hyphen after the complete word teoria, and the same preface later prints alla teoria stessa, so replacing the hyphen with a space restores the certain reading.
A stray intraline hyphen joins two complete words, and the parallel da essa determinato in the same sentence makes determinato dalla certain.

A non-planar developable of S4 has ∞¹ tangent planes, each lying in a pencil of hyperplanes that touch the surface along a generator, so these hyperplanes form an ∞² family; the exponent 1 is a certain slip, and correcting it leaves the contradiction with ∞³ intact.

printed: triplo per la curva doppia $C$ di $\Phi$
corrected: triplo per la curva doppia $\bar{C}$ di $\Phi$
justification: In the adjacent lines the double curve of Φ is C̄ while C denotes curves on F, so the bare C is a certain missing-bar error.
The components K̄1, K̄2, K̄3 belong to the double curve C̄ of Φ named in a) and b) just above, so the bar is certainly missing.

printed: la curva $\bar{K}_1$ proiettata nella medesima curva, bisogna che ogni retta congiungente un punto di $\bar{K}_1$
corrected: la curva $K_1$ proiettata nella medesima curva, bisogna che ogni retta congiungente un punto di $K_1$
justification: The curve that must keep the same projection, and whose points are joined to the line P2P3 so as to meet it again, is K1 on F as the surrounding clauses say, so both bars in this sentence are spurious and are removed together.
Two cone sections of order n meet on a surface of order m in mn² points, so the printed degree mn is a wrong calculation corrected by restoring the square.
The journal cited is the American Journal of Mathematics, so the German ending of Mathematik is a certain misprint in the title.
The 1935 article cited in the footnote is by S. F. Barber and O. Zariski, so the initial E. is a wrong letter with a certain correction.

printed: potranno essere contenuti anche in sistemi
corrected: potranno essere contenute anche in sistemi
justification: The subject is esse, the composite curves C+K, so the masculine contenuti is a certain agreement error for contenute.
The image Φ lies in S_R, as the opening paragraph and the subspaces of dimension R-r-1 and R-s-1 show, so the lowercase subscript is a certain index misprint.

printed: secante una curva \(C\) di \(|C|\) e un \(S_{R-s-1}\) della seconda, secante una curva \(K\) di \(|K|\)
corrected: secante una curva \(K\) di \(|K|\) e un \(S_{R-s-1}\) della seconda, secante una curva \(C\) di \(|C|\)
justification: By the preceding paragraph the S_{R-r-1} of the first series cut the K and the S_{R-s-1} of the second cut the C, and the projection that follows puts K in an S_{s-1} and C in an S_{r-1}, so the two curve labels are certainly swapped.
The curve created by transforming O_2, which is the one that appears twice in ω+ω_1+2ω_2, is ω_2, so the subscript 1 is a wrong index whose correction is certain.

Note 2 explains a branch issuing from O_1 and cannot support the mention of Enriques's theory of singularities, which belongs to the Enriques–Chisini note printed as 3, so the marker after Enriques and its link should read 3.
Zariski's co-author of the 1935 American Journal of Mathematics paper (doi 10.2307/2372025) is S. F. Barber, so only the wrong initial E. is replaced, as at p. 24.

printed: l. c. Ann. Journ. of Math., 1935
corrected: l. c. Amer. Journ. of Math., 1935
justification: The Barber–Zariski paper appeared in the American Journal of Mathematics and not in an Annals, so the wrong abbreviation Ann. becomes Amer. and the rest of the citation stays as printed.
All the other entries read ∂(φφ_i)/∂x_j and the determinant is formed from derivatives of the products, so only the opening parenthesis is moved after ∂.
The first-row expansion reproduces the three 4×4 determinants, and the Euler substitution yields −nf, only if the last column is +∂f/∂x_j throughout, so the minus before ∂f/∂x_3 is removed.
The final i of punti is missing and the intended word is certain.
The genitive identifying the system of plane sections is delle, as in the parallel phrases on the same page, so dalle is a one-letter misprint.

printed: della serie canonica e dello \(r\)-plo della serie caratteristica.}
corrected: della serie canonica e dello \((r-1)\)-plo della serie caratteristica.}
justification: By adjunction the curves of |(rC)′|=|C′+(r−1)C| cut on C the canonical series plus (r−1) times the characteristic series, as the formula in the same sentence shows, so r-plo is a certain off-by-one slip for (r−1)-plo.

printed: dello \(r\)-plo della serie caratteristica, ma tranne
corrected: dello \((r-1)\)-plo della serie caratteristica, ma tranne
justification: Second occurrence of the same off-by-one wording: the degree 2π−2+(r−1)n printed in the same sentence requires the (r−1)-plo of the characteristic series.
Quadrics through a′ cut the quartic F_4 residually in curves of order 8−1=7, which the same page calls C_7, so the subscript 4 is a certain error for 7.

printed: il sistema completo delle $C_4$ senza punti base
corrected: il sistema completo delle $C_7$ senza punti base
justification: The same residual system 2H−a′ (genus 6, dimension 6, degree 10) is printed again with subscript 4 instead of 7.
The fundamental point of the plane transformations is the point A of the branch curve named in this sentence and the next, not the projection centre O.
The words are transposed in print, and the parallel phrase i−1 volte per A_1 fixes the intended order i volte per A.
The cremonian transformation is of the fourth order, so the printed preposition dal is a one-letter typesetting error for del.
The neighbourhood represented by θ is that of the point O, so the feminine questa is a one-letter error for questo.
The degree of θ is the signed quantity ν=θθ=−1 (p. 86, −θθ=−ν=1 and the closing ν=−1), so the minus in grado −ν is a slip, while the ν_i keep their own convention.
For |C|=|C_1+θ| the genus formula needs the genus π−1 of C_1 and no primed quantity is defined, so the printed stroke (recorded as a prime for doubt N49 in task 1) is dropped.
With θθ=ν the computation (θ_0+θ_1)²=−ν_0−ν_1+2=−1 yields ν, not −ν, as −ν=1 above and ν=−1 below confirm, so only the leading sign is changed.
The section of a Φ_{n−4} together with a line has order n−3, the adjoint order for the plane sections (as on p. 84), so the second subscript n−4 is a slip for n−3.
The double plane arises by projecting F_4 from the point O at infinity, so del is a one-letter error for dal.

The surface z²=f(xy) has order 2n, so its biadjoints have order 2·2n−8=4n−8 (a surface of order 2n−8 cannot have a (2n−2)-fold point), and only the index is corrected while the multiplicity 2n−2 stands.
The letter r is missing from superficie.
The antecedent is the masculine fascio, so essa is a one-letter error for esso.

printed: sono eguali a zero e suoi poli debbono
corrected: sono eguali a zero e i suoi poli debbono
justification: The definite article i is missing before suoi poli.
The pronoun refers to the masculine plural i punti doppi, so contenerle is a one-letter error for contenerli.
Again the antecedent is the masculine plural punti doppi, so contenerle is corrected to contenerli.

printed: la \(C\) offre alle \(\Phi\) che debbono contenerle
corrected: la \(C\) offre alle \(\Phi\) che debbono contenerla
justification: The surfaces must contain the single curve C, so contenerle is corrected to contenerla, the form printed on p. 104.

printed: la curva gobba \(C\), d’ordine \(n\) e genere \(p\)
corrected: la curva gobba \(C\), d’ordine \(m\) e genere \(p\)
justification: The curve C has order m and the surfaces have order n (cf. nm−p+1 in the same sentence), so d’ordine n is a slip for d’ordine m.
Only the single totality of the surfaces Φ_n of order n is meant, so alle is a one-letter error for alla.
The genus π=π_1 is that of the plane sections of the surface F (s is only the order of the cutting surfaces), so the letter s is a slip for F.
The preceding expression for π_s has +s(s−1)n/2, and the binomial identity holds only with that sign (both sides equal (n−1)² at s=2), so the printed minus is a wrong sign.
The sentence describes the sum of the canonical series (LL') and the series cut by |C|, so the parallel construction requires della, a one-letter error.
Simplifying n+(p^(1)−1)+4π−4−2n gives 4π−5−n+p^(1), and the following relation π−1=n'−π'+1 holds only with n, so the prime on the last n is wrong.

printed:
p_a+\pi_s-1,
\]
che a sua volta sega
corrected:
p_a+\pi_{s+1}-1,
\]
che a sua volta sega
justification: The adjoints Φ_{n−3+s} cut the adjoint of the (s+1)-fold system, whose dimension is p_a+π_{s+1}−1 by the formula of §3 (as the stated order 2π−2+sn and the ratio π+sn+s(s−3)/2 confirm), so the index must be s+1.
The plural participle costrette and the sense (a system of surfaces) require delle superficie, a one-letter error.
With the indexing of p. 115 corrected, the adjoints of order n−3+(h−2) cut the adjoint of the (h−1)-fold system, so the genus index must be h−1.

The adjoints of order n−3+(h−3) have virtual dimension p_a+π_{h−2}−1 increased by both deficiencies, so the shifted index and the missing −1 must both be repaired (Stampa N70 records only the latter).
The sum just displayed begins with δ_0, the deficiency of the adjoints of order n−3, so the range must start at s=0.
Two series of dimension π−2+n sharing a series of dimension π−1 have a minimal sum of dimension π−3+2n, against π−2+2n for the complete series of order 2π−2+2n, so both n need the coefficient 2.
The surface is called F throughout and no object f is ever introduced, so the lower-case letter is an error for F.
The word sezione is broken at a printed line end without a hyphen, and the corrected text simply rejoins it.
As on p. 118, the lower-case f stands for the surface F, which is denoted by the capital letter everywhere else.
In the postulation formulas d is the order of the double curve and n the order of the surface, so the empty double curve of formal genus ϱ=1 has d=0.
Linear systems are always written between bars, including |C̄| in the very next clause and |L̄|=|L−θ|, so the missing delimiters around C̄ are supplied.
Since θ is fundamental for |C| and has degree −ν, n̄=(C−θ)²=n−ν, so the relation must read n=n̄+ν.
The genus of C=C̄+θ is π=π̄+ϱ+ν−1, so the bar over the left-hand π is spurious.
The footnote's large system |D| is the growing multiple |L_s|=|sL| (as in §8), whereas |L_1| would be |L| itself, so the subscript 1 is an error for s.

printed: maggiore della dimensione delle serie completa
corrected: maggiore della dimensione della serie completa
justification: The article must agree with the singular 'serie completa', so the single wrong letter of 'delle' is corrected to 'della'.
Substituting the preceding values of n_s and π_s in r_s ≥ p_a+n_s−π_s+1 gives p_a+s²n/2+sn/2−sπ+s, so the printed bound is a wrong calculation in a formula with a certain intended result.
The name is hyphenated everywhere else and only the internal hyphen was lost at the line break Rie-/mannRoch, so its restoration is certain.

printed: i caratteri, genere e grado, del primo sistema
corrected: i caratteri, grado e genere, del primo sistema
justification: In every adjacent formula, and in the author's usual order, n_1 is the degree and π_1 the genus, so the two swapped words are restored as 'grado e genere'.
Segre's work on ruled surfaces cited here (part II of the Recherches générales) appeared in Math. Annalen 34 in 1889, so the wrong year of the bibliographic reference is corrected.
The series cut on C by |K| has projective dimension p−1−i, as the Noether formula r=p+n−π+1−i that follows requires, so the exponent p−i is corrected to p−i−1.

printed: qualora non sia abbia, per qualche valore
corrected: qualora non si abbia, per qualche valore
justification: The extra letter in 'sia' is a plain misprint and the intended 'non si abbia' is certain.
The degree of L is ν throughout and adjunction gives K·L=2ρ−2−ν, so the printed r is a certain misprint for ν.

corrected: sia \(A_1\), ha un numero non positivo
justification: The clause lacks its verb, and the following inequality A₁(A₂+B)≤0 fixes the sense, so the missing word ha is supplied.
The residual of CD is the series cut by L' on D (the canonical series of D=C+L is cut by C+L'), so the wrong letter C becomes D.
The elliptic pencil is represented by the pencil of the C₄, so the preposition must be dal, which is a one-letter correction.

printed: Le possibilità che il sistema canonico puro
corrected: La possibilità che il sistema canonico puro
justification: The singular verb costringe and the single possibility described (that |K| be reducible) require the singular article La, which is the smallest correction.
The singular article lacks its final l.
From p+n−π+1≤1 with p≥1 only n≤π−1 follows (as in the parallel deduction on p. 158), and this one-symbol correction leaves the ensuing argument intact.
The three degrees δ₁, δ₂, δ defined in the preceding paragraph are being enumerated, so the missing separating comma is supplied (without it δ₁δ₂ reads as a product).
The adjoint surfaces have order m₁+m₂−4, as everywhere else in this computation, so the sign before 4 is wrong.
The participle must agree with the plural serie (there is one series for each of the two pencils).
m₂=2s+2π₂−2−σ counts the intersections of C₂ with the residual curve L₁ (the σ points on χ having been removed), so the missing index 1 is supplied.
The participle must agree with the feminine subject L'equivalenza.
Each doubled C counts for 2π−2 nodal curves, as the preceding sentence states, and only with 2π−2 does the expression reduce to Δ+4(ϱ−1)(π−1)−4 once Π=nπ−n+1 is substituted.

printed: P. \textsc{Bonnesen}, \textit{Sur les séries linéaires triplement infinies de courbes algébriques sur une surface algébrique.} Bull. de l’Académie Royal des
corrected: T. \textsc{Bonnesen}, \textit{Sur les séries linéaires triplement infinies de courbes algébriques sur une surface algébrique.} Bull. de l’Académie Royale des
justification: The main text on the same page names T. Bonnesen, and the French adjective must agree with Académie, so the initial is corrected and Royal becomes Royale.
The expression for d is formula (3) on p. 174 (formula (2) gives δ+τ), and 'expressed by' requires dalla, so both the preposition and the cross-reference are corrected.
Expanding with C²=n, CK=2π−2−n and K²=p^(1)−1 gives a final −p^(1), which equation (6) retains, so the dropped term is restored.
Seven characters are announced but six are printed, and removing n, π, p_a, p^(1) from the eleven leaves δ, I, d, ϱ, Π, τ, t, so d is supplied.
The explicit expressions of I and d are formulas (1) and (3), while (2) gives only δ+τ, so the cross-reference is corrected to (3).
By the fourth formula A) the invariant is 3(n+6π)−k = 12p_a−3p(1)+33, whereas 3(n+6π−k) still depends on n and π, so the closing parenthesis is moved to follow 6π.
Zeuthen's initials are H. G. (Hieronymus Georg), the order the book itself prints on pp. 167 and 180, so G. H. is a certain transposition.

printed: diramazione $D$ della corrispondenza sopra $f$. Essa sarà in generale dotata di un certo numero di nodi a cui rispondono sopra $F$ gruppi di $n$ punti con due coincidenze distinte. Inoltre la $D$ possiederà
corrected: diramazione $d$ della corrispondenza sopra $f$. Essa sarà in generale dotata di un certo numero di nodi a cui rispondono sopra $F$ gruppi di $n$ punti con due coincidenze distinte. Inoltre la $d$ possiederà
justification: In this paragraph and its footnote the branch curve on f is d while D is the coincidence curve on F, so the two capitals naming the branch curve are certain slips for d.
Substituting s = 2(ϱ+ε+χ)−2−ν into 24(P_a+1) = 24n(p_a+1)+6ϱ−6+3s−2χ gives the final term −3ν, confirmed by −3N² on p. 188, so the dropped ν is restored.

printed: ove si calcoli i valore di $x$
corrected: ove si calcoli il valore di $x$
justification: The article has lost its final l, and il valore is the only possible reading.
The printed § II, 8 omits Cap. and puts the section sign before the chapter numeral, and the intended locator is certain from the identical reference Cap. II, § 8 at the top of the same page.
By Riemann–Hurwitz an n-sheeted line with 2m simple branch points has genus π = m − n + 1, the value formula B) gives for N = 2m, so the extra division by 2 is removed.
The initial consonants of su cui are transposed, and the intended relative phrase is certain.
The r after T is missing, and the intended Troveremo is certain.
Two plane curves of order n meet in n² points, so the order of the characteristic series is certainly n² − 2d − 3k and only the exponent is missing.

The displayed definitions give r = m − π + 1 and the infinitely near curves of a system of dimension r + ω cut a series of dimension r + ω − 1, so inserting − 1 is the smallest change that makes the equality true and yields the speciality index ω stated next.
The duplicated preposition and the singular curva are plain misprints, and deleting su (as the Stampa note proposes) and restoring curve is the smallest change to the evident reading.

printed: parziale con curva una \(L\) del sistema
corrected: parziale con una curva \(L\) del sistema
justification: The words curva and una are transposed, and the intended con una curva L is certain.

printed: per \(\omega = 0\) si riduce a quella di Noether
corrected: per \(\omega' = 0\) si riduce a quella di Noether
justification: The formula being specialized is written with ω′, so the condition is certainly ω′ = 0 and only the prime is missing.

printed: quelle con curve canonica d’ordine maggiore
corrected: quelle con curva canonica d’ordine maggiore
justification: Noun and adjective disagree, and the parallel una curva canonica shows that the intended reading is curva canonica, a one-letter change.

corrected: infinitamente vicino un altro punto triplo
justification: The elision apostrophe before the masculine altro is an orthographic error whose intended reading un altro is certain, and deleting it is the smallest change.

printed: ed equivale ad una parte \((n-1)\)-ma di \(L\)
corrected: ed equivale ad una parte \(n\)-ma di \(L\)
justification: Since the canonical curve is the fixed elliptic component counted n−1 times and the bicanonical curves are L plus that component counted n−2 times, L is n times the component, so the single wrong number n−1 is certainly n.
The same paragraph identifies the tricanonical curve with the branch curve D_9, whereas D_3 is the bicanonical curve, so the wrong index is certainly 9.
The assigned double points are O, the two tacnodes and their two infinitely near double points, five in all, as the formula 6·9/2 − 5·3 = 12 and the five double points of D_6 named on p. 245 confirm.
The missing t in sisema is a plain typographical omission whose reading sistema is certain.

printed: importa 6 condizioni (e non più) si deduce
corrected: importa 7 condizioni (e non più) si deduce
justification: The bound of 19 moduli comes from the 12 invariants of the rational surfaces with a triple point, so a triple point on a general F_n must cost 7 conditions (one for a double point and six more to make it triple), while the later 6 for an already nodal surface is right and stays.

printed: come quello di cui ci siano valsi innanzi
corrected: come quello di cui ci siamo valsi innanzi
justification: The subject of the reflexive verb is the authorial we (ci ... valsi), so siano is a one-letter misprint for siamo.
With the printed plural Flaechen, the locative after auf requires the dative plural article den, a one-letter correction that leaves the transliterated spelling Flaechen as printed.
The adjective in Lefschetz's English title is algebraic, so the extra s is removed, whereas the unclosed guillemet is a matter of punctuation and is left as printed.

printed: Sulla retta $OP$ vi sono tre punti singolari di $D_{2n}$, cioè $P$, $O$
corrected: Sulla retta $OB$ vi sono tre punti singolari di $D_{2n}$, cioè $B$, $O$
justification: In type II, which the footnote annotates, the 4-fold point is called B and the exceptional branch line is OB, so OP and P are certain misprints for OB and B, and the separate geometric problem is left to the commentary (A5-030).
The same relation is printed as P=2(p-1)+s+1 on the next page and is required by M=10p+s+8=8p+P+9, so the minus before the final 1 is a certain misprint.
Types I' and II' have no double fibres, so their bigenus is the case s=0 of P=2(p-1)+s+1 and agrees with P_i=i(p-1)+1, giving 2(p-1)+1.
Since p=n-2-s for type III is printed repeatedly on the same page, the number of variable lines through O is p-1=n-3-s, with the s fixed lines OA_i added separately.
A group of s+1 points in the plane has 2(s+1)-8=2(s-3) projective invariants, which is exactly the term used in the following total 5(2n-s)-6-6s+2(s-3)=10n-9s-12.

printed: fa parte semplicemente dal sistema canonico impuro
corrected: fa parte semplicemente del sistema canonico impuro
justification: Fare parte takes di, so dal is a one-letter misprint for del, and the intended reading is certain.
The exceptional line r is defined to pass through A, A_1 and B, while D lies off r, so the fixed line completing the conics must be AA_1B.

printed: Occorre considerare le $F_9$ che passano triplamente
corrected: Occorre considerare le $F_8$ che passano triplamente
justification: The canonical surface is F_8, which cuts on the cubic Φ_3 the curve 2C_12 of order 24 = 3·8, so F_9 is a wrong index.
The identity is between complete systems, as in the preceding |(2F)'|=|F|, so the bars around the right-hand F are missing.
The V_3^n of S_{n+1} lies here in S_{p-1}, so n=p-2, matching V_3^{p-2} and the order 3n=3p-6 in the same item.
Clifford's n≥2r, stated just before, with n=p^{(1)}-1 and r=p-2 gives ≥, as the conclusion p^{(1)}≥2p-3 requires.
The sentence introduces r base points, so the s of the bound is a wrong letter for the same count; the plus sign is right.
The bound just displayed for variable parts composed with a pencil, (p-1)(π-1)+1 with π≥3, gives 2p-1, so the sign is wrong.
A canonical system of dimension p-1 maps into S_{p-1}, where a surface with rational hyperplane sections has the stated order p-2, so S_{p-2} is a wrong index.
For a branch decic the canonical images are all the ∞^5 conics, so p=6, as p^{(1)}=2p-3=9 also requires.
For p=2n+1 the minimum p^{(1)}=2p-3 being stated gives 4n-1, while 4n-2 is the degree K^2.
For p=2n-2 the minimum p^{(1)}=2p-3 gives 4n-7, while 4n-8 is K^2 after contracting the two (-1)-curves over the line joining O to the 6-fold point.
For p=2n the minimum p^{(1)}=2p-3 gives 4n-3, while 4n-4 is the degree K^2.
The construction makes F a canonical surface of S_{p-1}, as the statement on the preceding page says, so S_{p-7} is a wrong index.
In this paragraph the plane images are primed (C'_14, C'_7(O^4O_1^3)) and the curves of Φ_2 unprimed, so the plane system C_7(O^5O_1^2) has lost its prime.
The only possible referent of the pronoun is the feminine double curve C_7, so esso is a one-letter agreement error for essa.
A preposition is missing before the ambient-space symbol and is supplied as di, as in le F_9 di S_4 in the next paragraph.
The surfaces of order 9 are the agent of segato, as in segato su Φ_4 dalle superficie a few lines below, so delle is a misprint for dalle.
A system can be contained only in the system |F|, written with bars just before and after in the same sentence, so the bars are missing.
Serie is invariable but the adjective autoresidue and the verb possono are plural, so the article la is a one-letter misprint for le.
The phrase 'coi medesimi caratteri' refers back to Segre's sextic with p=4 and p^(1)=9, and a canonical quadric counted four times has degree 8, so the intended 9 is certain.
The middle term lacks the factor z that appears in the two parallel equations and that the weighted degree and the discriminant 4p_8^3+q_12^2 require.
The syntax requires the conjunction e, so the accent printed over it (kept in the diplomatic text) is removed here.
The double quadric cone with branch curve C_10 is the bicanonical model found in §14 for p=2 (an ∞³ system, P=4), so p=1 is a misprint for p=2.
Both summands are cubics and the same composite surface is written F_3+F'_3 a few lines above, so the index 2 is a misprint for 3.
The only model in §16 is the tricanonical F_9 described just before, and its moduli are the ones being counted, so the subscript 8 is a misprint for 9.
The whole Osservazione concerns a triple cubic as tricanonical model, so bicanoniche is a misprint for tricanoniche.

printed: propria che è la la quartica \(K\)
justification: The article la is printed twice across a line break, so one occurrence is removed.
The quartic is said to be of genus 1 just above and on the next page, so genere 2 is a slip for genere 1.
The hyphen between the system and the verb sega is an extraneous printed mark with no mathematical meaning, so it is removed.
A net (P=3) has a characteristic series of dimension 1, and the same sentence derives P=6 from a g_8^4 by that same rule, so g_8^2 is a slip for g_8^1.
The verb porta has lost its initial p.

printed: diramazione \(C_{12}\) d’ordine 12, dotata di due punti quadrupli
corrected: diramazione \(C_{10}\) d’ordine 10, dotata di due punti quadrupli
justification: Type III is the double plane of pp. 314–315, whose branch curve is a C_10 of order 10 with two quadruple and two [3,3] points, so both 12s are misprints for 10.
The book itself prints carattere additivo on p. 311, so the doubled t is a misprint rather than an archaic spelling.

printed: ciò significa che il genere delle \(C\) vale
corrected: ciò significa che il genere delle \(C'\) vale
justification: The genus 7 = 4 + p^(1) + 3 − 1 is that of the adjoint curves C' projected as sextics with a triple point, whereas the C have genus 4, so the missing prime is restored.
The preceding sentence asserts ∞^p disequivalent curves for p_a=-p and the next line gives p_g-p_a=p, so the printed minus sign is a certain sign error for q≥p.

printed: colle fade suddette e non con
corrected: colle falde suddette e non con
justification: The omitted letter l is certain, since the passage speaks before and after of the same hypersurface sheets (falde).
One wrong letter spoils the idiom a dir vero, which the text itself uses on p. 338, so the intended reading is certain.

printed: Prendiamo le mosse da un questione
corrected: Prendiamo le mosse da una questione
justification: The feminine noun questione requires the article una, so the missing final letter is certain.
The omitted subscript is certain, since the parallel formula r'=p_a+ν-ϱ+1 and the dimension counts of §5 all use p_a.
The image of the g^{q-1}_{2p-2} was named K_{q-1} earlier in the same paragraph, so the printed M is a certain wrong letter for K.
The intersection is taken on M_{q-1}, as the preceding paragraph sets up, so the first subscript q-2 is a certain error for q-1, while the later M_{q-2} are correct.
The case was announced as 'poi al caso q=4' and parallels 'Supposto q=3', so the stray subscript g is removed.
The converse concerns surfaces of geometric genus zero, and with p_a=0 its conclusion p_a=-p (p>0) would contradict the hypothesis, so the subscript a is a certain error for g.
The Humbert reference is the third footnote of the page and is numbered (3) below, so the in-text call (1) is a certain error for (3).
The general formula has the factor (t_i−1), so a single multiple elliptic component has valence (t−1)(2ϱ−2)=0, and the plus sign is a misprint hidden by 2ϱ−2=0.
Riemann–Roch r ≥ p_a+n−π+1 with n=r²i and π=rϱ+r(r−1)i/2−r+1 gives +r and no final +1, so both members are corrected, since the sign-only change proposed in N247 would still overstate the bound by 1.
The conjunction e is needed to coordinate this clause with the preceding è chiaro che, so the accented verb is a misprint.

printed: le ipotesi II e 1 dette innanzi
corrected: le ipotesi II e I dette innanzi
justification: The hypotheses are labelled I and II (p. 391 has le ipotesi II e I), so the Arabic 1 is a typographical substitution for the Roman I.
The singular adjective s-bicanonica and the parallel phrase della serie s-bicanonica on the same page require della.
The comparison is with the π-th adjoint, as the next sentence and the parallel display on p. 392 show, so the superscript π is missing.
C is para-π-canonical, so its s-fold multiple is para-sπ-canonical, as the parallel passage on p. 392 states.
An extraneous hyphen joins the two separate words dato and con.
The parenthesis opened before Teorema is never closed, so one closing parenthesis is missing before the final stop.
The reduced group is 2K_1+…+2K_r+K_0 and the following virtual curve L'−K''−(K_1+…+K_r) has no unindexed K, so the extra K is a misprint.
The series ḡ+g has order 4π−4 and a quadricanonical double, and Enriques himself calls it semiquadricanonica on pp. 381 and 385.
Whether the glyph is a misprinted s or a damaged e, the intended word indipendentemente is certain.
The image curve of ḡ is K_{2π−2} earlier in the same paragraph, so the 2 of the subscript has dropped out.
The linear image of ḡ=g^{π−2}_{2π−2} is a curve of order 2π−2, which is written K*=K_{2π−2} lower on the same page.
The elements of the variety are the m series ḡ, while the canonical series g is unique, so the overbar is missing.
A non-special ḡ=g^{π−2}_{2π−2} has as its linear image a K_{2π−2} in S_{π−2}, as in the same construction on pp. 385 and 389.

corrected: sistema lineare ampio quanto si vuole
justification: The line-end hyphen wrongly joins the separate words si and vuole (cf. ampio quanto si vuole on p. 385).
The paragraph treats the failure of hypothesis I and passes to F* so that hypothesis I holds there (cf. p. 384), so II is a wrong cross-reference.
The example concerns normal sextics K_6 in S_5, whose order is m, while n counts the projectivities.

For the example exactly as specified (four horizontal cubics and six vertical generators of branching) the invariants are uniquely p_g=3 and p_a=2 (χ=3, q=1, the 24 crossings being rational double points), so only the two miscomputed numbers change.

printed: un contratto tripunto lungo tre generatrici
corrected: un contatto tripunto lungo tre generatrici
justification: An extra r turns the geometric term contatto into contratto, and the intended word is certain.
The Zeuthen–Segre identity is Δ=13+12p_a−p^(1), as on p. 395, and only the plus sign yields the following lower bound p_a≥−1.
The first branch value lacks the index 1 that the preceding product and the list of branch sections z=a_i give it.
The Riemann–Hurwitz right-hand side is 2n+2π−2, as in the corresponding equality on p. 404.
Since k_s=s−1−h_s with 0≤h_s≤s−1, the value k_s=s−1 must be admitted, and changing one symbol gives the justified bound without touching the argument.
Each branch value has n/s ramification points of index s, so the factor n/s printed on pp. 404 and 410 is restored.
Dividing the Riemann–Hurwitz equality by n with π≥1 gives Σ(1−1/s)≥2, the bound the following t=3 step needs; the printed ≥1 is a true but too weak slip of the author, not a misprint.
In this separate display the same bound must read t−Σ1/s≥2 for the chain to give Σ1/s≤1 when t=3.
Only the available bound Σ1/s≤t−2 yields the next display's Σ1/s≤1 for t=3, so the true but insufficient t−1 is replaced.
The fourth case treats s_1≥4 and the lower bound s_2≥3 presupposes s_1=3, so the third case must read s_1=3; the wrong casewise plurigenus values are left to the commentary.
The first multiplicity lacks its index 1, matching s_2 and s_3 in the same example.
The integer-part brackets of the general formula for P_m and of the following estimates are missing in this display.
There are t summands each at most 6, so the sum is bounded by 6t, not 24 (six indices equal to 2 already give 36).
With the bound 6t the chain becomes P_12≥6t−23=6(t−4)+1>1 for t≥5, so only the numbers derived from 24 change and the printed ≥ is kept.
The enumeration otherwise omits the admissible s_1=4, e.g. (4,4,4), so the strict sign becomes ≥ as in the case s_1≥4 on p. 409.
The h of the Italian plural pluricanoniche is missing, and the intended word is certain.
The product of two commuting second-kind involutions is a translation, a transformation di prima specie as in the preceding paragraph, so serie is a wrong word.
All neighbouring branch factors and the following deck-transformation formulas use z−b.
In the row of products by ω the cycle π→ω→τ→π (ζ6²·ζ6⁴=1) requires τω=π, whereas πω already equals ω_1 in the same row.

printed: rispondono a curve ellittiche \(C\) di \textit{modulo generale}
corrected: rispondono a curve ellittiche \(K\) di \textit{modulo generale}
justification: The moduli classified in §§ 17–18 belong to the curves K carrying the g_n^1, while the C are translation orbits of unrestricted modulus, so the letter must be K.

printed: a curve \(C\) \textit{armoniche}, ed infine \(III_a\) e \(III_b\) a un tipo \textit{ciclico} con \(C\) \textit{equianarmoniche}
corrected: a curve \(K\) \textit{armoniche}, ed infine \(III_a\) e \(III_b\) a un tipo \textit{ciclico} con \(K\) \textit{equianarmoniche}
justification: The harmonic and equianharmonic curves are the K of §§ 17–18 (curva K equianarmonica, p. 422), so both letters continue the wrong C of p. 424 and are corrected to K.
With multiple fibres of multiplicities (3,3,3) the formula of § 14, which Enriques cites for these values, gives P_4=0, so the printed 1 is a miscalculation.
The formula of § 14 gives P_4=0 for both III_b and III_c (canonical orders 6 and 3, neither dividing 4), so the digit in the shared row is corrected.
The theorem is H. A. Schwarz's and the running text on the same page spells the name Schwarz.
The surface throughout the argument is the capital F, and no lowercase f is defined in this section.
The French adjective, as in the title of the 1895 Comptes rendus note, is birationnelles.
The accented verb è before possiede is ungrammatical, and the conjunction e is certainly intended.
The point and gap are a defect of the type where n belongs, and the word is certainly eccezioni.
Since V_q lies in V_p with q<p, the subgroup is ∞^q inside the group ∞^p of V_p, as the next paragraph states with Γ_q in Γ_p.
The reduction of hyperelliptic surfaces to surfaces in a Jacobian variety is in Chapter IX § 9, cited as such on pp. 436–437, whereas Chapter X § 9 treats another subject.
The Severi formula for surfaces in (1,n) correspondence is in Chapter V § 8, so the printed locator 28 is a wrong cross-reference.
The curves L correspond to points of F but lie on Φ, as the next sentence (le ∞² L su Φ) states.
For a genus-two pencil with fibres of genus π the Euler number gives Δ−4+4(π−1), so the coefficient 8 is a calculation error, and the deductions p^(1)=1, Δ=0, π=1 still follow.
The participle refers to the singular un sistema bicanonico, parallel to di cui in the next clause, so the plural is an agreement misprint.
The noun conseguenza governs di here, so dalla is a one-letter misprint for della.
The base term is non-negative, so the relation must read Δ−4 ≤ 12p_a−p^(1)+9 for the chain to give p_a ≥ −1, and the reversed sign is corrected.
The corrected first line with Δ ≥ 0 gives 12(p_a+1)−p^(1)+1 ≥ 0, the only form consistent with the stated case p_a=−1, p^(1)=1, so reversing ≤ alone (N305) is insufficient.
The limiting case of p_a ≥ −1 is p_a = −1, so the dropped minus sign is restored.
The surfaces with all genera one are treated in Cap. VII §2, as cited on pp. 447 and 450, and the book has no Chapter XII.
The adjective must agree with the plural ordini, so quale is a one-letter misprint for quali.
Volume IV of the Lezioni is Libro VI, as in the book's other citations of cap. III §§35–39, so the book number is corrected to VI.
Section 40 opens on p. 246 of Vol. IV (after §38 on p. 234 and §39 on p. 242), so the printed pag. 24 has lost its final digit.
The elided preposition lacks its apostrophe, so d ordine is corrected to d’ordine.
The Enriques–Severi memoir in Acta Mathematica is titled Mémoire sur les surfaces hyperelliptiques, so the y is a spelling error.

printed: che abbiamo distinti in sette tipi
corrected: che abbiamo distinte in sette tipi
justification: The participle refers to the feminine plural superficie, so distinti is a one-letter misprint for distinte.
The eight finite families (the regular sextic type and the seven elliptic types) form class B'' as defined above, so the label needs a second prime.

printed: le superficie \(B')\) contengono sempre fasci di curve ellittiche e perciò si ravvicinano alle superficie \(C)\), in confronto alle \(B'')\)
corrected: le superficie \(B'')\) contengono sempre fasci di curve ellittiche e perciò si ravvicinano alle superficie \(C)\), in confronto alle \(B')\)
justification: By the definitions above, the B'' surfaces always contain elliptic pencils while the B' surfaces in general do not, so the two labels are interchanged.
The Notizia on the transcendental inequality begins on p. 461 while p. 463 begins §9, so the page reference is corrected.

printed: In questo caso abbiamo veduto (Cap. X, \S~4)
corrected: In questo caso abbiamo veduto (Cap. XI, \S~4)
justification: The case p_a=−1, p_g=1 was treated in §4 of this chapter, cited as Cap. XI §4 a few lines above, so only this occurrence is corrected.
The examination of bicanonical curves for regular surfaces is in Cap. VIII §§18–20, within the §§14–20 of Cap. VIII cited in the next paragraph.
The plurigenera that distinguish the seven types are P_2, P_3, P_4 and P_6, so the repeated final P_4 is corrected to P_6.
